title: The GoT challenge
description:
Transferring from Slack convo.

The GoT data in repurrrsive comes from an API but for teaching purposes, after I wrangle it into the list that ships with the package, I transform it *back* into JSON and XML files that also ship with the package.

The current script below `data-raw/` uses an experimental branch of xml2 I created before xml2 had a nice function for this. I implemented `as_xml()` and the moral equivalent in xml2 today is `as_xml_document()`. But I can't just drop it in there.

https://github.com/jennybc/repurrrsive/blob/7ecc79f9a6b1925996ec20d78f0291d91451db31/data-raw/got_pov-chars-wrangle.R#L5-L7

https://github.com/jennybc/repurrrsive/blob/7ecc79f9a6b1925996ec20d78f0291d91451db31/data-raw/got_pov-chars-wrangle.R#L116-L120

``` r
> got_chars %>%
+   #xml2:::as_xml() %>%
+   as_xml_document() %>% 
+   as.character() %>% ## workaround to get explicit UTF-8 encoding
+   read_xml() %>%
+   write_xml(here("inst", "extdata", "got_chars.xml"))
Error: Root nodes must be of length 1
```

I haven't looked at this lately but I think there's either a buglet in `as_xml_document()` or a UI/documentation gap. It would be nice if I could reproduce the XML already in repurrrsive with current xml2 functions. This is a little detective adventure for someone.

title: Support for prefixed names in writing xml nodes
description:
Dear all, i'm in the process to migrate from XML to xml2 a series of packages i'm maintaining. Although for some dealing with single namespace, the task is relatively easy (i started with [geosapi](https://github.com/eblondel/geosapi), i'm now looking at packages where XML schemas include various namespaces, such as  [atom4R](https://github.com/eblondel/atom4R) (as starter) to then move towards more complex ones like [geometa](https://github.com/eblondel/geometa). 

In this context, the practice is to use prefixed element names instead of element names made of local parts only coupled with repeating `xmlns` attributes.

I didn't find the way to do that in xml2, although it's possible with XML with `xmlOutputDOM` / `nameSpace` argument. I tried with `xml2::xml_set_namespace` but it doesn't have any effect.

Is it a missing feature? If not, could you give me an example.

Thanks a lot
Emmanuel

title: Optimize xml_path() and xml_find_all() for large node sets
description:
`xml_path()` and `xml_find_all()` can spend substantial time in wrapper-side work when operating on large node sets.

I have a local branch with two general optimizations, both intended to preserve existing semantics:

1. Speed up `xml_path()` for large `xml_nodeset`s by caching reusable ancestor paths within a single call.
2. Speed up `xml_find_all.xml_node()` materialization by avoiding an unnecessary duplicate pass for single-context XPath node sets and reducing per-node R object construction overhead.

Is this a direction you would be open to reviewing as a PR?

Isolated benchmark results from my local machine:

- `xml_path()` on a synthetic node set with 124,001 nodes:
  - before: ~0.77s
  - after: ~0.07s

- `xml_path()` on a large real-world XML bundle with 415,022 selected nodes:
  - before: ~2.43s
  - after: ~0.28s

- `xml_find_all()` / XPath result materialization on large attribute result sets:
  - synthetic 300k attributes: roughly 1.5-2x faster in the materialization-heavy path
  - real-world XML bundle, `//@*`, 155,009 attributes: roughly 1.6-2x faster in isolated runs

The changes are not specific to any particular XML schema or downstream package. They target repeated ancestor path construction and large XPath result materialization.

I added regression tests comparing batch `xml_path()` output to per-node `xml_path()` output, and checking that single-context `xml_find_all()` XPath node sets remain unique.

title: read_html(url) double-encodes UTF-8 on Windows (codepage 65001)
description:
- Reproducer: Non-ASCII chars get double-UTF-8-encoded when passing a URL to read_html(). Passing the same HTML as a string works correctly.

- Regression: Works in xml2 1.3.6, broken in 1.5.2. Likely introduced in 1.3.7 (switch to Rtools libxml2) or 1.3.8 (libxml2 update to 2.11.5).

- Environment: R 4.5.2, Windows, l10n_info()$UTF-8 == TRUE, codepage 65001.

```r
# Minimal reproducible example: xml2::read_html(url) double-encodes UTF-8 on Windows
# Environment: R 4.5.2, Windows, l10n_info()$`UTF-8` == TRUE, codepage 65001
# xml2 version: 1.5.2 (works correctly in 1.3.6)
 
library(xml2)
 
url <- "https://translate.google.com/m?tl=de&sl=en&q=apples"
 
# --- Method 1: read_html(url) - BROKEN ---
page1 <- read_html(url)
node1 <- xml_find_first(page1, "//div[@class='result-container']")
result1 <- xml_text(node1)
 
Encoding(result1)
#> [1] "UTF-8"
charToRaw(result1)
#> [1] c3 83 c2 84 70 66 65 6c
#> Expected: c3 84 70 66 65 6c ("Äpfel")
#> Actual:   c3 83 c2 84 70 66 65 6c (double-encoded UTF-8)
result1
#> [1] "Ã\u0084pfel"
 
# --- Method 2: read_html(string) - WORKS ---
resp <- curl::curl_fetch_memory(url)
html <- rawToChar(resp$content)
Encoding(html) <- "UTF-8"
page2 <- read_html(html)
node2 <- xml_find_first(page2, "//div[@class='result-container']")
result2 <- xml_text(node2)
 
Encoding(result2)
#> [1] "UTF-8"
charToRaw(result2)
#> [1] c3 84 70 66 65 6c
result2
#> [1] "Äpfel"
 
```

title: "Memory allocation failed" error for truncated xml/html input on recent libxml2 versions
description:
In xml2 v1.3.6 the following commands worked on macOS, Linux and Windows (notice the missing ">" at the end of the string):

```
tmpText <- "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"utf-8\"?><Biotic xmlns:xsi=\"http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-ins\""
res <- read_html(tmpText)
```

In xml2 v1.3.7 and v1.3.8 I get the following error on Windows:

```
"Memory allocation failed"
```

When completing the block by ">", I do not get the error:

```
tmpText <- "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"utf-8\"?><Biotic xmlns:xsi=\"http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-ins\">"
res <- read_html(tmpText)
```

title: `read_xml` crashes R when trying to read from an `archive::archive_read` connection if the connection is closed beforehand
description:
I've been handed a database in which one of the fields contains XML documents as compressed blobs (ZIP/PK archives). Rather than writing the file out to disk every time and reading it in using `read_xml` I tried using the `archive` package's bindings to libarchive to read it directly. It works great except that I'm trying to close the connections properly afterward and learned that R crashes if I incorrectly close the rawConnection object before calling `read_xml`.

```r
xml_text <- '<text>Hi</text>'
blob <- charToRaw(xml_text)

blob_con <- rawConnection(blob)
spec_con <- archive::archive_read(blob_con)
close(blob_con)
xml2::read_xml(spec_con)
```

The error I get when R crashes is:

```
Error in (function (con, rw = "")  : invalid connection
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'cpp11::unwind_exception'
  what():  std::exception
```

I honestly don't know whether this is an `archive` problem or an `xml2` problem so happy to repost there, I just don't know enough about the internals to learn where the problem itself is and `read_xml` is what's currently causing the crash when called.

I'm on R 4.5.1 with xml2 1.3.8 and archive version 1.1.12.

title: `read_xml(x)` throws an error if `x` is a `textConnection()`
description:
Currently I observe that `read_xml(x)` throws an error if `x` is a `textConnection()`.

```r
library("xml2")
s <- '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n<outer>\n<inner>Inner</inner>\n</outer>'
con <- textConnection(s)
x <- read_xml(con)
```
```r
Error in readBin(3L, "raw", 65536L) : 
  can only read from a binary connection
```

I'm aware you could use `x <- read_xml(paste(readLines(con), sep = "\n"))` as a workaround but this seems like an easy case to support.  

I'm putting together a pull request that adds a `read_xml.textConnection()` S3 method.

title: error "start tag expected" from quartz
description:
On MacOS, plotting anything (base, grid, etc) and then invoking the OS "Print" dialog with the `xml2` package loaded causes R to emit an error and all following GD operations to fail.

It emits this error on macos via `R` in a shell or in emacs/ess. It does _not_ emit the error on macos in RStudio (does not use `quartz()`), nor anywhere on linux. I have not verified Windows, though I suspect not since it uses `x11()` and not `quartz()`.

```r
library(xml2)
plot(1)
### switch to the graphics window, try to print with Cmd-P or File>Print

# Error: Start tag expected, '<' not found [4]
```

If we plot first, load `xml2`, then go back to the window, the result is the same. If I load xml2 and then `detach("package:xml2")`, it fails in the same way.

Once it has failed, that graphics window becomes unresponsive (mac's spinning rainbow-wheel). I can `dev.close()` it and `dev.list()` is now empty, but the window remains. No new graphics devices can be opened, so in essence this R process's graphics days are done. Starting a new R process works fine.

If I load xml2 and then `detach("package:xml2", unload=TRUE)` and invoke the Print dialog,

```r
Selection: 
 *** caught bus error ***
address 0x104a3a0c0, cause 'invalid alignment'

Possible actions:
1: abort (with core dump, if enabled)
2: normal R exit
3: exit R without saving workspace
4: exit R saving workspace
```

I tried this with the three packages imported by `xml2` individually and combined, and it did not trigger an error. This leads me to believe that it is either in `xml2` itself or somehow in the linking with `libxml2`.

I've confirmed it does this on macos 15.5, R-4.4.3, xml2_1.3.8, one two separate MBPs; another R-SIG-Mac user verified it on macOS Sonoma 14.7.6, R 4.5.1 RC (unknown xml2 version).

This came up recently on R-SIG-Mac (https://stat.ethz.ch/pipermail/r-sig-mac/2025-July/015229.html), and one user helped narrow it down so far to `xml2`.

title: Vectorising XPath expressions
description:
I regularly find myself searching XML documents for multiple unique entries among the children of a parent node. I have a handcrafted function that vectorises over the names of the entries and it thus makes separate calls to the XML library for each name; see simplified function below.

Would it be possible to vectorise at the level of the C++ code, rather than in R? I would imagine that the performance would be much better than the serialised calls I have in my code below.

```r
# Argument `names` is a character vector
find <- function(names) {
  xp <- paste0("//entry[@id='", names, "']")
  
  # Vectorise this call to `xml_find_first()`, rather than the `lapply()` that I am using now
  nodes <- lapply(xp, function(nm) xml2::xml_find_first(my_xml_document, nm))

  # Process any nodes that were retrieved
  found <- which(sapply(nodes, class) == "xml_node")
  if (length(found)) {
    nodes <- nodes[found]
    cu <- sapply(nodes, function(n) xml2::xml_text(xml2::xml_find_first(n, "canonical_units")))
    desc <- sapply(nodes, function(n) xml2::xml_text(xml2::xml_find_first(n, "description")))
    data.frame(name = names[found], units = cu, description = desc)
  } else NULL
}

```

title: Build process on Linux includes shared libraries not in library path.
description:
When building xml2 on Linux (tested with RHEL7 and R 4.1,4.2,4.3), the compile and link steps will include libraries associated with directories in $PATH, but which aren't in the library search path for anything else.  For example, if conda is in use, we have /optnfs/common/miniconda3/bin in $PATH.  Building xml2 finds and uses header files in /optnfs/common/miniconda3/include/ and library (.so) files in /optnfs/common/miniconda3/lib  (explicitly passed to linker with -L option).  The compile succeeds, but then the test load fails with a missing library.  Disabling conda makes the build locate the library in one of the default places (/usr/lib64) and it works.

The first library affected in libicui18n.so, but there are many other duplicated libraries between the standard system location and private copies installed by applications.

title: Is NaN the right value for xml_find_num() of an absent XPath?
description:
Encountered when trying to convert some `as.integer(xml_find_num())` usage. Consider:

```r
x1 <- xml2::read_xml('<NODE line1="1">x</NODE>')
x2 <- xml2::read_xml('<NON-NODE line1="1">x</NON-NODE>')

xml2::xml_find_num(x1, "number(//NODE/@line1)")
# [1] 1
xml2::xml_find_num(x2, "number(//NODE/@line1)")
# [1] NaN
xml2::xml_find_int(x2, "number(//NODE/@line1)")
# Error in `xml2::xml_find_int()`:
# ! Element at path `number(//NODE/@line1)` must be a whole number, not `NaN`.
# Run `rlang::last_trace()` to see where the error occurred.
xml2::xml_find_first(x2, "//NODE/@line1")
# {xml_missing}
# <NA>
```

I would have expected `NA` to show up from `xml_find_num()` if `xml_find_first()` is returning `xml_missing`.

Either way, the inconsistency of `xml_find_int()` should be fixed. Since `as.integer(NaN)` is `NA_integer_`, shall we return that directly instead of looking at `check_number_whole()`?

title: Duplicated names for elements in list after calling `as_list`
description:
Thanks for your work on `xml2`!

Consider the following reprex where I have an xml document with multiple nodes of the same element (`item`):

``` r
a <- xml2::as_xml_document("<collection><item>foo</item><item>bar</item></collection>")
b <- xml2::as_list(a)

## This will only show "foo" but not "bar"
b$collection$item
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "foo"

## However both elements are there:
names(b$collection)
#> [1] "item" "item"
b$collection[[1]]
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "foo"
b$collection[[2]]
#> [[1]]
#> [1] "bar"
```

<sup>Created on 2023-12-30 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

When the xml document in the reprex is converted to a `list`, the list elements will have duplicated names. Which I think is undesirable in R, and will cause all sorts of problems. Would it be possible to either:

1. Throw a warning when `as_list` produces duplicated element names; or
2. Repair the names such that they become unique.

Thanks for considering.

title: print.xml_nodeset very slow for document with one huge node
description:
Found in the XML representation of an edge case R file:

```r
library(xml2)
library(xmlparsedata)

p = parse("https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mwaldstein/edgarWebR/fb9a38e6a57186ffd1c93cc1aa00c4fdf1bc5514/tests/cache/browse-edgar-11457c.R")
xml = read_xml(xml_parse_data(p))
```

Printing this is painfully slow:

```r
system.time(print(xml))
# {xml_document}
# <exprlist>
# [1] <expr line1="1" col1="1" line2="5944" col2="43" start="145" end="855979">\n  <expr line1="1" col1="1" line2="1" col2="9" start="145" end="153">\n    <SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL li ...
#    user  system elapsed 
#   2.906   0.048   2.958 
```

Took a brief look, it looks like `encodeString()` is the culprit:

```r
# ** debugging inside show_nodes() **
system.time(vapply(x, as.character, FUN.VALUE = character(1)))
#    user  system elapsed 
#   0.248   0.017   0.268 
system.time(encodeString(vapply(x, as.character, FUN.VALUE = character(1))))
#    user  system elapsed 
#   2.959   0.024   3.007
```

Is it possible to apply `substr()` twice -- once after `as.character()`, then again after `encodeString()`?

```
chr = vapply(x, as.character, FUN.VALUE = character(1))
nchar(chr)
# [1] 18965721
```

This is clearly already wayyy to wide (`width = 180` for me).

I _believe_ we can always just apply

```r
x %>%
  substring(1, n) %>%
  encodeString() %>%
  substring(1, n)
```

since the default behavior of `encodeString()` is to simply add `\` to non-printable characters, so it will just be a weakly wider version of the input.

Happy to file a PR if that sounds good.

title: Trim all xml_text results from a nodeset at the same time
description:
`xml_text` can take a long time when used with a large nodeset when `trim` is `TRUE`, and most of that time is spent calling `sub` twice for each node.  One experience I had was getting the text for a nodeset with about 4.5 million nodes, where `Rprof` showed that calls to `sub` made up 72% of the nearly two minutes spent in `xml_text`.

I'll happily make a pull request if you'd like

Here's a brief demo showing time saved:

```r
library(xml2)
library(microbenchmark)

blob <- paste0(c("<x>", rep("<y> Hi </y>", 1000), "</x>"), collapse = "")
tree <- read_xml(blob)
y_tags <- xml_find_all(tree, "//y")

xml_text_sub_after <- function(x, trim = FALSE) {
  res <- vapply(x, xml_text, trim = FALSE, FUN.VALUE = character(1))
  if (isTRUE(trim)) {
      res <- sub("^[[:space:] ]+", "", res)
      res <- sub("[[:space:] ]+$", "", res)
  }
  res
}

microbenchmark(
  as_is = xml_text(y_tags, trim = TRUE),
  proposed = xml_text_sub_after(y_tags, trim = TRUE),
  check = "identical"
)
# Unit: milliseconds
#      expr     min      lq      mean   median       uq     max neval
#     as_is 35.2209 35.9433 37.787917 36.64865 38.15000 58.4016   100
#  proposed  6.7719  6.9522  7.625734  7.16715  7.40195 16.2116   100
```

title: Should XPtr(T* p) call R_PreserveObject(data_) as XPtr(SEXP x) does?  The destructor calls R_ReleaseObject in either case.
description:
In xml2/inst/include/xml2_types.h there are two constructors for XPtr.  One, XPtr(SEXP x), calls R_PreserveObject(data_) and one, XPtr(T* p), does not.  The destructor calls R_ReleaseObject(data_) in either case.  TERR notices that R_ReleaseObject was called for a non-protected object and R does not.

E.g., foghorn::cran_details("bit64") causes 157 complaints from TERR that R_ReleaseObject was used on an extptr that was not protected by R_PreserveObject. 

My question whether XPtr(T* p) should be protecting the external pointer it creates?  I don't have an example of R freeing an external pointer's data too early, but I haven't worked that hard to come up with one.  I am removing the warning from TERR now but was wondering if it caught a real problem.

title: libxml2 2.9.13 changes recovery mode
description:
This is more of a note on html processing, in case you are not aware. libxml2 v2.9.13, which is the newest release that gets pulled in by apt on Ubuntu 22.04, changes how the "recovery" mode works for html rendering. Since xml2 is used by many other packages (like kableExtra and modelsummary), this may end up being a repeated issue. See the following code: ```R xml2::read_html("* pval < 0.05; ** pval < 0.01") ``` For systems that have libxml2 v.2.9.12 or before installed, the output is as expected: ``` {html_document} [1]

* pval < 0.05; ** pval < 0.01

``` For systems that have libxml2 v.2.9.13 installed, it's truncated at the first less than sign: ``` {html_document} [1]

* pval

``` This is a result of the upstream devs reducing recovery mode processing to avoid DDoS attacks and generally simplify processing. They also indicate in the issue linked below that this functionality is likely to continue. There's an argument to say that `xml2`, like `libxml2`, should just be concerned with processes "correct" html/xml and users should not rely on consistent recovery mode or error handling, but this also seems like a change that will affect a lot of folks doing statistics. https://gitlab.gnome.org/GNOME/libxml2/-/issues/339

title: read_xml "NOWARNING" option does not suppress namespace warnings
description:
The "NOWARNING" options states it should suppress warning reports from the libxml2 parser. It does not suppress warnings about the namespace prefix on nodes. 

The use-case here is the [WordProcessingML from Microsoft's Open XML SDK](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/office/open-xml/working-with-paragraphs).

```r
xml2::read_xml("<w:t></w:t>", options = "NOWARNING")
#> Warning in read_xml.raw(charToRaw(enc2utf8(x)), "UTF-8", ..., as_html =
#> as_html, : Namespace prefix w on t is not defined [201]
#> {xml_document}
#> <w:t>
```

title: xml2 is not removing namespaced attributes
description:
Possibly related to [340](https://github.com/r-lib/xml2/issues/340). 

The [xml2 Node Modification vignette](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/xml2/vignettes/modification.html) states that using `NULL` as the value will remove the attribute completely. In the example below, the 'space' attribute in `doc1` is correctly removed using this method. However, the 'xml:space' attribute in `doc2` is not getting removed using this method. 

```r
library(xml2)
doc1 = as_xml_document('<xml><t space="preserve">1</t><t space="preserve">2</t></xml>')
doc1_children = xml_children(doc1)
xml_attrs(doc1_children) <- NULL
print(doc1_children)
#> {xml_nodeset (2)}
#> [1] <t>1</t>
#> [2] <t>2</t>

doc2 = as_xml_document('<xml><t xml:space="preserve">1</t><t xml:space="preserve">2</t></xml>')
doc2_children = xml_children(doc2)
xml_attrs(doc2_children) <- NULL
print(doc2_children)
#> {xml_nodeset (2)}
#> [1] <t xml:space="preserve">1</t>
#> [2] <t xml:space="preserve">2</t>
```

title: url_absolute fails with spaces in url
description:
`xml_attr(x, "href")` returns un-encoded URLs if that's how they appear in the source, but then those URLs fail in `url_absolute`. 

``` r
url <- "/filename with spaces.pdf" 
xml2::url_absolute(
  url,
  base = "https://example.com/"
)
#> [1] NA
xml2::url_absolute(
  utils::URLencode(url),
  base = "https://example.com/"
)
#> [1] "https://example.com/filename%20with%20spaces.pdf"
```

<sup>Created on 2023-08-23 with [reprex v2.0.2](https://reprex.tidyverse.org)</sup>

`url_absolute()` gets confused if the URL contains spaces, and silently returns NA. This should at least warn the user, but it might be preferable to deal with it directly.

This is where I found it in the wild:

``` r
base_url <- "https://www.copyright.gov/fair-use/fair-index.html"

pdf_urls <-
  rvest::read_html(base_url) |> 
  rvest::html_element("table") |> 
  rvest::html_elements("tr>td:first-of-type>a:first-of-type") |>
  rvest::html_attr("href")

pdf_urls[[10]] |> 
  rvest::url_absolute(base_url)
#> [1] NA

pdf_urls[[10]] |> 
  utils::URLencode() |> 
  rvest::url_absolute(base_url)
#> [1] "https://www.copyright.gov/fair-use/summaries/ONeil%20v.%20Ratajkowski%20No.%2019%20CIV.%209769%20(S.D.N.Y.%202021).pdf"

title: xml_descendants() as akin to xml_child()/xml_children() and equivalent to xml_find_all(., "descendant::*")
description:
Follow-up to #8.

Consider trying to find the minimal indentation of expressions in an R file (using the AST via {xmlparsedata}). I'll use `dbplyr/tests/testthat/helper-src.R` for illustration:

```r
library(xmlparsedata)
library(xml2)

xml <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tidyverse/dbplyr/1e48cfaf795f9101792567bc68ce7d24a19db9d5/tests/testthat/helper-src.R" |>
 parse() |>
 xml_parse_data() |>
 read_xml()
```

##### Objective: comment calls to `test_register_con()`, _besides_ the `RSQLite` one, with the _correct indentation_

```r
xpath <- "
//SYMBOL_FUNCTION_CALL[text() = 'test_register_con']
    /parent::expr
    /parent::expr[not(.//SYMBOL_PACKAGE[text() = 'RSQLite'])]
"

exprs <- xml_find_all(xml, xpath)
```

The part about indentation requires examining the `col1` attribute for all descendant nodes of `exprs`. Here's how we can do this currently:

```r
col1s <- vapply(
  exprs,
  \(expr) min(as.integer(xml_attr(xml_find_all(expr, ".//*"), "col1"))),
  integer(1L)
)
```

If we have `xml_descendants()`, this can be a tad cleaner + more readable:

```r
col1s <- vapply(
  exprs,
  \(expr) min(as.integer(xml_attr(xml_descendants(expr), "col1"))),
  integer(1L)
)
```

title: as_list() return element text as character, not list
description:
### Issue Description
`as_list()` will convert element text into a list of length 1 with a single character element. I would expect it to "simplify" or "unbox" the text so it is not a list. The **XML** package already has this type of behavior in using `xmlToList()`.

### Reproducible Example
In the example below the "bar" element text "Hello" is represented as a list. I would expect it to be a character string.
```r
library(xml2)
as_list(read_xml("<bar>Hello</bar>")) 
#> $bar
#> $bar[[1]]
#> [1] "Hello"

# the desired result would be
#> $bar
#> [1] "Hello"
```

The **XML** package has similar style to the more desirable behavior. 
```r
library(XML)
xmlToList(newXMLNode("bar","Hello"))
#> [1] "Hello"
```

title: .copy = FALSE argument in xml_add_child does not move the element
description:
As the documentation of `xml_add_child` suggests, setting `.copy = FALSE` moves the element to its new location. However, it does not remove the node from its original location, leaving a zombied node that cannot be removed.
```
R version 3.6.3 (2020-02-29)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
Running under: Windows 10 x64 (build 18362)
xml2_1.3.1
```

## Case 1
``` r
# Create a simple document
doc <- xml2::as_xml_document(
  "<document>
    <body>
    </body>
  </document>"
)
body <- xml2::xml_find_all(doc, "//body")[[1]]

# Create an element named "a" in the document
a <- xml2::xml_add_child(doc, "a")
# Move it to body
a_moved <- xml2::xml_add_child(body, a, .copy = FALSE)

# We see it is copied by reference
a$node
#> <pointer: 0x0000000008a32e40>
a_moved$node
#> <pointer: 0x0000000008a32e40>

# We see it now lives in two places, but we find only one as there is only one
cat(as.character(doc))
#> <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
#> <document>
#>   <body>
#>     <a/></body>
#>   <a/>
#> </document>
xml2::xml_find_all(doc, "//a")
#> {xml_nodeset (1)}
#> [1] <a/>

# This should remove 'both' of them
xml2::xml_remove(a)

# But only removes the "a" at the location we wanted to move it to
cat(as.character(doc))
#> <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
#> <document>
#>   <body>
#>     </body>
#>   <a/>
#> </document>
xml2::xml_find_all(doc, "//a")
#> {xml_nodeset (1)}
#> [1] <a/>

# Removing it again
xml2::xml_remove(a)

# It is now zombied, because we cannot remove it.
cat(as.character(doc))
#> <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
#> <document>
#>   <body>
#>     </body>
#>   <a/>
#> </document>
xml2::xml_find_all(doc, "//a")
#> {xml_nodeset (1)}
#> [1] <a/>
```


## Case 2
Whenever namespaces are involved, `xml_find_all` creates an error, I guess it produces an infinite loop somewhere.

``` r
# Create a simple document
doc <- xml2::as_xml_document(
  "<document xmlns:z=\"https://example.com/\">
    <z:body>
    </z:body>
  </document>"
)
body <- xml2::xml_find_all(doc, "//z:body")[[1]]

# Create an element named "a" in the document
a <- xml2::xml_add_child(doc, "z:a")
# Move it to body
a_moved <- xml2::xml_add_child(body, a, .copy = FALSE)

# We see it is copied by reference
a$node
#> <pointer: 0x00000000047eaea0>
a_moved$node
#> <pointer: 0x00000000047eaea0>

# We see it now lives in two places, but trying to find the first, or all, crashes
cat(as.character(doc))
#> <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
#> <document xmlns:z="https://example.com/">
#>   <z:body>
#>     <z:a/></z:body>
#>   <z:a/>
#> </document>
xml2::xml_find_first(doc, "//z:a")
#> Error in xml_find_first.xml_node(doc, "//z:a"): Memory allocation failed : growing nodeset hit limit
#>  [2]
xml2::xml_find_all(doc, "//z:a")
#> Error in xml_find_all.xml_node(doc, "//z:a"): Memory allocation failed : growing nodeset hit limit
#>  [2]
```

title: Error with kableExtra::column_spec() might involve xml2
description:
A recent [question on StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/65419443/kableextra-column-spec-error-maybe-dplyr-summarise) describes the following error:

```
library(tidyverse)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

Summary <- mtcars %>% 
            group_by(cyl, gear, carb) %>% 
            summarise(count = n(), .groups = "keep") %>% 
            arrange(desc(cyl))

kable(Summary, caption = "mtcars Data Summary\n", align = c('l','l','c','c')) %>%
                  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped","hover"),full_width = FALSE, position = "left") %>% 
                  collapse_rows(columns = 1, valign = "top") %>% 
                  column_spec(1, width = "3cm") %>% 
                  column_spec(2, width = "3cm") %>% 
                  column_spec(3, width = "2cm") %>% 
                  column_spec(4, width = "2cm")

# Error in xml_children(x)[[search]] : subscript out of bounds
```
The code works as expected until the last `column_spec` call, which produces the error. There's also an unsolved [`kableExtra` issue](https://github.com/haozhu233/kableExtra/issues/513) that seems to be similar to this and that may be [related to the `xml2` package](https://github.com/haozhu233/kableExtra/issues/513#issuecomment-704011589).

I thought I would report these errors here in case this is a bug in the `xml2` package. If not, do you have any ideas on what's going wrong and whether there might be a workaround?

title: xml_find doens't see added attributes with namespaces
description:
I'm trying to modify xml by adding child nodes with attributes, and then I'm looking for the subset of added nodes with attributes I just added:

```r
library(xml2)
doc <- read_xml('<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?><bookstore xmlns:xxx="https://www.w3.org/"><book name="Harry Potter 1"></book></bookstore>')

node <- xml_find_first(doc, "book")
xml_add_child(node, .value="link", "xxx:resource"="http://harry_potter.com")

# Now, will try to find the node just added:
xpath <- "//book/link[@xxx:resource=\"http://harry_potter.com\"]"

# results 1:
xml_find_all(doc, xpath)
# nothing found: {xml_nodeset (0)}
# that's wrong

# saving to temporary file and loading from it:
write_xml(doc, "temp.xml")
doc <- read_xml('temp.xml')

# using same query again, results 2:
xml_find_all(doc, xpath)
# the results are correct and link is found
```

The bug is related to namespaces. If the added child node and query doesn't have xxx: namespace, the output is correct, and results 1 contain the node that was added.

title: Documentation needed: Creation of root node with namespace
description:
As of [Release 1.2.1.](https://github.com/r-lib/xml2/releases/tag/v1.2.1) it seems to be possible to assign a namespace to a newly created root node, using `xml_root()`

Unfortunately this is not documented at all, neither under `?xml_root` (redirecting to `xml_children`) nor under `xml_new_root()` (redirecting to `xml_new_document`), so that it is not clear how to use it. The parameters `ns`, `prefix`, `uri` don't work as expected.

Importing the namespace from an existing XML document does also not work. And creating an object of class `xml_namespace` from scratch seems also impossible.

Is there a solution?

Thanks

title: Is it possible to get comment content in a node?
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
Unsure if comment contents are parseable and addressable.

I see that `xml_comment()` will add comments to a xml document, and you can specify the comment contents.  I was wondering if comment content text was also parseable, as I have some structure where the person stuck information in comments after certain nodes, and it would be nice to get the text of those comments.  From the simple parsing example below, it looks like the comments get addressed, but their textual contents are not stored.  Am I missing anything, or is this as per design?

### Reproducible Example
``` r
x <- xml2::read_xml("<fruits><apple color = 'red' /><!-- mycomment --></fruits>")
x
#> {xml_document}
#> <fruits>
#> [1] <apple color="red"/>
xml2::as_list(x)
#> $fruits
#> $fruits$apple
#> list()
#> attr(,"color")
#> [1] "red"
#> 
#> $fruits[[2]]
#> [1] "[ comment ]"
```



<details>
<summary>Session Info</summary>

``` r

title: xml_path() shows asterisks and numbers in brackets instead of names
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result

I'm expecting output from `xml_path()` to show the xml path hierarchy in words, not asterisks and numbers in brackets.

I'm expecting code like this

```
doc %>% xml_find_all('//*')  %>% xml_path()
```

to yield results like this:

```
[1] "/Return"                              
[2] "/Return/ReturnHeader"                 
[3] "/Return/ReturnHeader/ReturnTs"        
[4] "/Return/ReturnHeader/TaxPeriodEndDt"  
[5] "/Return/ReturnHeader/TaxPeriodBeginDt"
```

instead of output like this: 

```
[1] "/*"        "/*/*"      "/*/*/*[1]" "/*/*/*[2]" "/*/*/*[3]"
```

Also, queries don't work as expected, such as:

```
xml_find_all(doc, "//TaxPeriodBeginDt")  
```

The above gives this result

```
{xml_nodeset (0)}
```

when the expected result is

```
{xml_nodeset (1)}
[1] <TaxPeriodBeginDt>2016-01-01</TaxPeriodBeginDt>
```

### Reproducible Example

```
library(tidyverse)
library(xml2)
```

**problem case**

```{r}
s <- 
'<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<Return  xmlns="http://www.irs.gov/efile" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://www.irs.gov/efile" returnVersion="2016v3.0">
  <ReturnHeader binaryAttachmentCnt="0">
    <ReturnTs>2017-07-05T19:04:21-05:00</ReturnTs>
    <TaxPeriodEndDt>2016-12-31</TaxPeriodEndDt>
    <TaxPeriodBeginDt>2016-01-01</TaxPeriodBeginDt>
  </ReturnHeader>   
</Return>     
'
```

**OK case**  but XML file must be modified before reading

If I delete “xmlns=”http://www.irs.gov/efile" from the `<Return>` element `xml_find_all` works as expected.  (I deleted all three assignments in the `<Return>` element in this "OK" example.)

```{r}
s <- 
'<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8"?>
<Return  returnVersion="2016v3.0">
  <ReturnHeader binaryAttachmentCnt="0">
    <ReturnTs>2017-07-05T19:04:21-05:00</ReturnTs>
    <TaxPeriodEndDt>2016-12-31</TaxPeriodEndDt>
    <TaxPeriodBeginDt>2016-01-01</TaxPeriodBeginDt>
  </ReturnHeader>   
</Return>     
'
```

**Processing**

```{r}
doc <- read_xml(paste(s, collapse = "\n"))  # easier way to do this?
```

```{r}
doc %>% xml_find_all('//*')  %>% xml_path()
```

```{r}
doc %>% xml_find_all('/Return/ReturnHeader/*')  %>% xml_path()
```

```{r}
xml_find_all(doc, "//TaxPeriodBeginDt")  
```

<details>

Millions of XML files are online [IRS 990 public documents](https://docs.opendata.aws/irs-990/readme.html), which could be parsed using xml2 or other tools.

Here's a complete file used to create the example above: 
https://s3.amazonaws.com/irs-form-990/201701869349300035_public.xml

This is an awkward workaround:

```{r}
xml_find_all(doc, "//*[name() = 'TaxPeriodBeginDt']")  
```

title: feature request: read_html, read_xml.character argument to always parse the string directly
description:
When parsing a string that possibly contains HTML, `read_html` attempts to read the character string as a file if it does not contain any html tags: 

```
read_html('asfd')
Error: 'asfd' does not exist in current working directory ('...').
```

This comes from `read_xml.character` where the following dispatch takes place:
```
 if (grepl("<|>", x)) {
        read_xml.raw(charToRaw(enc2utf8(x)), "UTF-8", ..., as_html = as_html, 
            options = options)
    }
```

It would be nice if the user could control this behavior with an argument, e.g. to always force `read_html` to attempt to parse a string as raw HTML instead of a path. This would also solve the problem above that arises with the solution given in [this stackoverflow answer](https://stackoverflow.com/a/34344957/786220).

title: xml_url does not work (at least in combination with base_url)
description:
The behavior of `xml_url` appears to have changed pretty drastically in v1.3.0.

Previously, passing `base_url` via `read_html` resulted in it setting the url returned by `xml_url`

These are deeply simplified examples but highlight the change in behavior. I can work around the change from "NA" to "<CHARSXP: NA>", but the loss of the xml_url is a big loss which will require a bit of re-architecting. 

This breaks edgarWebR (currently off CRAN due to vignettes making remote API calls)

### Using string input
**Example 1**
```r
require(xml2)
doc <- read_html("<html/>", base_url = "http://test.com")
xml_url(doc)
```
On v1.2.5 the output was "http://test.com"
On v1.3.1 the output is "UTF-8"

**Example 2**
```r
require(xml2)
doc <- read_html("<html/>")
xml_url(doc)
```
On v1.2.5 the output was "NA"
Ov v1.3.0 the output is "UTF-8"

### Using httr response
**Example 3**
```r
require(xml2)
require(httr)
href <- "https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/cik_lookup?company=cloudera"
res <- GET(href)
doc <- read_html(res, base_url = href)
xml_url(doc)
```
On v1.2.5 the output was "https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/cik_lookup?company=cloudera"
Ov v1.3.0 the output is "<CHARSXP: NA>"

**Example 4**
```r
require(xml2)
require(httr)
href <- "https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/cik_lookup?company=cloudera"
res <- GET(href)
doc <- read_html(res)
xml_url(doc)
```

title: xml_ns doesn't  retrieve the namespace of a single node
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
<!--Example: `read_xml()` fails on the following input.-->

I think the implementation of `xml_ns` is non-intuitive. When called on a node `xml_ns` retrieves all namespacess of the root document. What I think it should do is to return the namespace of the current node.

### Reproducible Example

```r
library(xml2)
     x <- read_xml('
      <root>
        <doc xmlns:x1 = "http://foo.com" xmlns:x2 = "http://bar.com">
            <x1:element/>
            <x2:element/>
         </doc>
      </root>
     ')

xml_ns(xml_find_first(x, "//x1:element"))
# x1 <-> http://foo.com
# x2 <-> http://bar.com
xml_ns(xml_find_first(x, "//x2:element"))
# x1 <-> http://foo.com
# x2 <-> http://bar.com
>

title: Function to extract HTML tables
description:
Hello, thanks for developing the package.

Is developing a table extracting function from HTML files something planned for the `xml2` package?

In the `rvest` package, the `rvest::html_table` function attempts to accomplish this task, but is still very slow and has consistency issues in the data structure. I pointed this out to [issue 273 of the rvest package](https://github.com/tidyverse/rvest/issues/237)

In the `XML` package, the `XML::readHTMLTable` function does the job of extracting tables (at least in the tests I did), with good data speed and consistency.

Table extraction in HTML files is apparently not trivial. There are other interesting packages like [htmltab](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/htmltab/index.html) that try to cover this gap in the R ecosystem.

A function for this purpose would be very useful. The `rvest` package has 1,083 stars in github (the third most voted package in the repository), but its development is slower than other TidyVerse packages and relies heavily on `xml2`. In addition, a function for this purpose would help in the [Migration guide for XML package](https://github.com/r-lib/xml2/issues/246).

Thanks for listening.

title: read_xml: parsing error with a CDATA section

title: Error on creating new XML - Expecting an external pointer

When trying to create a new XML body and it has a namespace defined on the root node, xml2 returns an error, even that the namespaces are correctly assigned. It just happens with the root node.                         "xmlns:xsd" = "http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema",
                        "xmlns:soap12" = "http://www.w3.org/2003/05/soap-envelope") %>%

title: xml_attr()<-is mishandling xml_nodesets
description:
When assigning a character vector to an xml_nodeset using `xml_attr()<`-, the first element in the vector is assigned to all nodes. This is different than, e.g., `xml_text()<-`, which allows different values to be assigned to different nodes.

### Reproducible Example
```r
library(xml2)
x <- read_xml("<x><a b='c'/><a b='d'/></x>")
a_set <- xml_find_all(x, "a")
# Doesn't work as expected
xml_attr(a_set, "b") <- c("e", "f")
xml_attr(a_set, "b")
#> [1] "e" "e"
# Also doesn't work as expected
xml_set_attr(a_set, "b", c("g", "h"))
xml_attr(a_set, "b")
#> [1] "g" "g"
```

I understand that `xml_attrs()` can be used to set the same attribute for multiple nodes. However, since the current behavior is (IMO) unexpected I believe it should at least be reflected in the documentation.

title: Add as_xml_document method for data.frame
description:
### Issue Description
It is tedious to create valid XML from a data.frame. Currently, `as_xml_document()` chokes on a variety of hacks: 

```
dat <- head(iris,3)

as_xml_document(dat)
Error in UseMethod("as_xml_document") : 
  no applicable method for 'as_xml_document' applied to an object of class "data.frame"

as_xml_document(list(dat))
Error in UseMethod("xml_text<-") : 
  no applicable method for 'xml_text<-' applied to an object of class "xml_document"

as_xml_document(as.list(dat))
Error: Root nodes must be of length 1

as_xml_document(list(iris=as.list(dat)))
Error in node_append_content(x$node, value) : 
  Expecting a single string value: [type=character; extent=3].
```

### Reproducible Example
The best example I could find was on SO [How to convert dataframe to xml using xml2 package?](https://stackoverflow.com/a/45929603/5258043), but this seems hacky as well. There are some assumptions about the element names that could be provided by arguments, but here is an example of the desired logic:

**Current**
```
dat <- head(iris,3)
dat_xml <- lapply(purrr::transpose(dat),
                  function(x) {

title: xsd comment causes node to be empty
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
I use the xml2 package to read xsd files, which perfectly work on the first ones I worked with (https://github.com/NCEAS/eml). But I wanted to give a try with the standard "Observation & Measurement" and its xsd specification (http://schemas.opengis.net/om/2.0/observation.xsd). It happens that this has a comment inserted in an element ("phenomenonTime") and parsing it with the `read_xml` function and then turning it into a list with `as_list` renders an empty node (contains a `list()`). 

### Reproducible Example
You can try to download the file "observation.xsd" (link above) and just execute the following lines:
```r
library(xml2)
x <- as_list(read_xml("observation.xsd"))
View(x)
# this didn't work for me
```
and then edit "observation.xsd" to remove the comment in "phenomenonTime". Then it worked for me.

I don't think I already saw this issue posted before but I might have skipped it.

I enclose a session where I 
- define a DTD and a XML example file 
- read the XML with the package `XML` that works as expected: the field `field1` contains `'Han Oostdijk Quantitative Consultancy'` i.e. the resolved entity `hoqc` with the nested entity `author` defined in the DTD. 
- do the same with package `xml2`.  I have commented out the line ` c1 = xml2::xml_find_all(w2,"//field1")` because this is the line that causes the abortion of the R session.

- use package `xml2` but replace the line in the XML with the entity `hoqc` by `<field1>&author;</field1>`. This works as expected: results in the string `'Han Oostdijk'`.

title: slow performance when creating moderately large XML files
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
I need to create codebooks for social science datasets (typical number of variables above 5-600). Before xml2, I used the base function cat() with good results. xml2 seems like a much better alternative and gave it a shot... but it takes about 15-16 seconds per dataset while creating the same XML file with sink() and cat() doesn't take more than 4-5 seconds.

### Reproducible Example

Below you can find a trimmed down example that on my computer takes about 8 seconds to create the XML file. In the real situation, there are many more nodes and attributes to create (some depend on other logical conditions), but this is the bottleneck.

Example:
```r
library(xml2)
missing <- c(-1, -2, -3)
values <- c("Very weak" = 1, "Weak" = 2, "Middle" = 3, "Strong" = 4, "Very strong" = 5, "Don't know" = -1)

root <- xml_new_document()
codeBook <- xml_add_child(root, "codeBook")
dataDscr <- xml_add_child(codeBook, "dataDscr")

for (i in seq(600)) {
    var <- xml_add_child(dataDscr, "var", name = paste("V", i, sep = "_"))
    
    if (TRUE) { # something needs to be checked here, as an example
        xml_attr(var, "nature") <- "ordinal"
        xml_attr(var, "representationType") <- "text"
    }

    labl <- xml_add_child(var, "labl")
    xml_text(labl) <- paste("Variable label for V", i, sep = "_")

    for (v in seq(length(values))) {
        ismiss <- is.element(values[v], missing)
        catgry <- xml_add_child(var, "catgry")
        if (ismiss) xml_attr(catgry, "missing") <- "Y"
        catValu <- xml_add_child(catgry, "catValu")
        xml_text(catValu) <- as.character(values[v])
        labl <- xml_add_child(catgry, "labl")
        xml_text(labl) <- names(values)[v]
    }
}

write_xml(root, "test.xml")
```

Is there a way to speed things up?

  xml2::read_xml(httr::content(x, "raw"), encoding = encoding, base_url = x$url,
    as_html = as_html)
}
```

i.e. check that the request succeeded, and pass the url along to `base_url`

title: _R_CHECK_LENGTH_1_LOGIC2_
description:
With current *R-devel*, we can use the experimental environment variable `_R_CHECK_LENGTH_1_LOGIC2_` to detect code where `&&` or `||` encounter arguments of length more than one.
For **xml2**, I see
```R
Sys.setenv("_R_CHECK_LENGTH_1_LOGIC2_" = TRUE)
xml2::read_html("<html><title>Hi<title></html>")
#> Error in is.null(arg) || !nzchar(arg) : 
#>   'length(x) = 3 > 1' in coercion to 'logical(1)'
traceback()
#> 3: parse_options(options, xml_parse_options())
#> 2: read_html.default("<html><title>Hi<title></html>")
#> 1: xml2::read_html("<html><title>Hi<title></html>")
```

I stumbled upon this problem when R-devel CMD checking my own packages in an environment with enabled `_R_CHECK_LENGTH_1_LOGIC2_`:

Register classes with setOldClass
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result

It is not possible to use the class `xml_document` or `xml_node` in formal definitions of S4 classes.
It would be helpful for packages using S4 if they could properly define slots as being of a type provided by this package.

This should be possible with [`setOldClass`](https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/methods/versions/3.5.2/topics/setOldClass).

(Let me know if you'd welcome a PR on this.)

library(xml2)

setClass("Testclass",
         representation(xml = "xml_document"),
         prototype = list(xml = xml2::xml_missing()),
         validity = function(object) {
           #...
           return(TRUE)
         }
)
```

title: OS X Yosemite Issue with Homebrew and Solution
description:
I'm not sure how useful you will find this, but this might at least help with some support.

The issue is that it appears that pkg-config --cflags libxml-2.0 tends to return a nonexistent directory, namely /usr/include/libxml2.  This seems to occur on at least 7 macs between my own and some friends, all running yosemite.

The fix is to just search the libxml directory of homebrew before trying pkg-config.  The directory location should be sufficiently obscure not to impact other operating systems.

``` bash
# Custom libxml2 path for compatibility with old XML package
if [ "$LIBXML_INCDIR" ]; then
  LIBXML_CFLAGS="-I$LIBXML_INCDIR"
  echo "User specified xml2 headers in $LIBXML_INCDIR."
# slightly annoying fix for homebrew / OSX
elif [ -r "/usr/local/opt/libxml2/include/libxml2/libxml/parser.h" ]; then
  LIBXML_CFLAGS="-I/usr/local/opt/libxml2/include/libxml2/"
  LIBXML_LIBS="-L/usr/local/opt/libxml2/lib -lxml2"
elif [ "$PKGCONFIG" ]; then
  LIBXML_CFLAGS=`pkg-config --cflags libxml-2.0`
  LIBXML_LIBS=`pkg-config --libs libxml-2.0`
elif [ -r "/usr/include/libxml2/libxml/parser.h" ]; then
  LIBXML_CFLAGS="-I/usr/include/libxml2/"
elif [ -r "/usr/local/include/libxml2/libxml/parser.h" ]; then
  LIBXML_CFLAGS="-I/usr/local/include/libxml2/"
elif [ -r "/opt/csw/include/libxml2/libxml/parser.h" ]; then
  LIBXML_CFLAGS="-I/opt/csw/include/libxml2/"
  LIBXML_LIBS="-L/opt/csw/lib/ -lxml2"
fi
```

title: Return xml_missing for missing nodes
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
Although I talked with Jim at useR! in Brisbane about it and he said, that this wouldn't make its way into the package, I will give it a try nevertheless, since I cannot wrap my head around it, that there is no better solution. 

My goal is representing the content from an XML-file in a `data.frame`. To this end, I am extracting some of the elements. The problem is that the nodes are of different types, and their children don't have the same structure. In the below example, some have a `<publisher>` node, some don't. 

My solution is to `purrr::map` over the nodes to keep the same structure for all children. But this is obviously not as efficient, as it could be. Am I missing something obvious and/or would it be possible to implement something like this on a lower level (C) that is faster?

### Reproducible Example

```r
library(xml2)
library(purrr)
library(dplyr)

'<ref-list>
  <ref id="ref1">
      <citation type="book">
        <title>Some title</title>
        <publisher>Some publisher</publisher>
      </citation>
   </ref>
   <ref id="ref2">
      <citation type="journal">
        <title>Another title</title>
        <volume>1</volume>
      </citation>
   </ref>
</ref-list>' -> xml

xml <- read_xml(xml)

# only elements that are present are extracted, thus the lengths
# differ.
xml_find_all(xml, ".//title") %>% xml_text()
#> [1] "Some title"    "Another title"
xml_find_all(xml, ".//volume") %>% xml_text()
#> [1] "1"
xml_find_all(xml, ".//publisher") %>% xml_text()
#> [1] "Some publisher"

extract_element <- function(x, xpath) {
  out <- xml_find_all(x, xpath) %>% xml_text()
  
  if (is_empty(out)) out <- NA_character_
  
  out
}

xml %>% 
  xml_find_all("ref") %>% 
  map(~{
    list(title = extract_element(., ".//title"),
         volume = extract_element(., ".//volume"),
         publisher = extract_element(., ".//publisher"))
  }) %>% 
  bind_rows()
#> # A tibble: 2 x 3
#>   title         volume publisher     
#>   <chr>         <chr>  <chr>         
#> 1 Some title    <NA>   Some publisher
#> 2 Another title 1      <NA>

title: Parsing time (XML to data.frame)
description:
Posted following on StackOverflow - but may be more relevant here (since it is package-specific):
Converting OIOIUBL invoices from XML to a dataframe in R I am using the code below (sample XML-file is in the link further down).

When iterating over 323.859 files the XML-to-dataframe parsing takes 64 minutes. From the code below how could this be optimized? The same task using Python takes ~6 minutes (sorry for being unable to share the Python-code).

I am aware that R is not good at moving lots of data in-memory. But can the difference of 58 minutes in execution time be attributed to this or my lacking programming skills?

Example:
```r
library(xml2)
readinvoice <- function(nextfile) {
    tryCatch(doc <- read_xml(nextfile, options = c("RECOVER", "HUGE")),
            error = function(e) {print(paste("Error in code", basename(nextfile), e$message))})
    art <- xml_name(doc)
    path <- xml_path(doc)
    ID <- gsub('\\.xml', "", basename(nextfile))
    priceTotal <- xml_double(xml_find_all(doc, "./cac:LegalMonetaryTotal/cbc:PayableAmount"))
    tryCatch(df <- data.frame(cbind(art, path, ID, priceTotal)),
            error = function(e) {print(paste("Error in code", bilagsident, e$message))})
    }
xmlfilelist <- list.files("PATH/TO/FILES", full.names = TRUE)
result <- lapply(xmlfilelist, readinvoice) # THIS LINE IS SLOW
```
Link to sample file: https://1drv.ms/u/s!Am4CDwbz-dfchPZKhf9RQPSfnKcLeg

Thanks for any help you may provide.

Best regards,
Mikkel

title: xml_new_root should accept an xml_namespace object
description:
Hey @jimhester, 

I could be missing something, but it seems a bit clumsy that to define namespaces when calling `xml_new_root` there's no simple way to pass an existing `xml_namespace` object.  For instance, the vignette gives us the following example:

```r
d <- xml_new_root("sld",
    xmlns = "http://www.o.net/sld",
    "xmlns:ogc" = "http://www.o.net/ogc",
    "xmlns:se" = "http://www.o.net/se",
    version = "1.1.0") 
```

There's no simple way to read the namespaces from an existing doc and pass them to `xml_new_root()` or `xml_new_doc` as far as I can tell. 


We can get the namespaces back as an `xml_namespace` object:

```r
ns <- xml_ns(d)
class(ns)
```

but as far as I can tell, things get pretty cludgy if we want to pass this to `xml_new_root`:

```r
names(ns) <- paste("xmlns", names(ns), sep=":")
do.call(xml_new_root, c(.value = "root", as.list(ns)))
```

Is there a way to do this without the `do.call` and manual pasting `xmlns` and all?  Maybe `xml_new_root` & friends could be tweaked to take an `xml_namespace` object as argument directly?  Thanks!

title: Feature request: Combined read_html/write_html function
description:
If you are scraping a website, it is good practise to download the page once and store a copy, so you don't have to keep re-downloading it.

That means that it is easy to end up with lots of code like

```r
page <- read_html(url)
write_html(page, "somefile.html")
```

It seems like it would be useful to have a single function (`save_html()` perhaps) to do both operations.

The dumbest implementation is something like this:

```r
save_html <- function(x, file) {
  page <- read_html(x)
  message("Writing to ", force(file))
  write_html(page, file)
  invisible(page)
}
```

It needs a bit of fleshing out to deal with `...` args to `read_html()` and `write_html()`, to it would be nice to have a default filename generated from the URL.

title: read_html error in read_connection_ with HTTP 1.0 redirects
description:
### Issue Description and Expected Result
I am making a request to a site that returns a 301 redirect error over HTTP 1.0 protocol with  Connection: close . read_html (and other xml2 methods) fail with a message like this:

```
Error in read_connection_(x, n) : 
  Failure when receiving data from the peer
```

However, if I create the connection with file(), redirects are followed correctly. Similarly download.file follows redirects and setting libcurl option followlocation=TRUE in RCurl also 
works. 

At least some HTTP redirects _are_ followed correctly, so this was confusing.

Wrapping the URL with file() is a simple workaround, but it took me a while to figure that out.

### Reproducible Example
Example:
```r
library('xml2')
library('RCurl')

# This produces an error currently
x <- read_html('https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc29275/m1/129')

# These work
x <- read_html(file('https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc29275/m1/129'))
y <- getURL('https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc29275/m1/129', .opts=c(followlocation=TRUE))
z <- readLines('https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark:/67531/metadc29275/m1/129')

# Note that this works, so redirects are followed sometimes (HTTP 1.1 & keepalive)
read_html('http://httpbin.org/redirect-to?url=http://httpbin.org/html?status_code=301')
```

I don't have another http 1.0 redirecting endpoint. In case that one changes, the headers returned are

```
HTTP/1.0 301 MOVED PERMANENTLY
Date: Wed, 19 Jul 2017 20:55:54 GMT
Server: Apache/2.2.15 (Red Hat)
Content-Length: 0
Location: https://digital.library.unt.edu/ark%3A/67531/metadc29275/m1/129/

Connection: close
Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8
```

title: No way to set the value of an attribute to the empty string
description:
It doesn't seem to be possible to set the value of an attribute to the empty string. This is valid XML and there's no problem parsing such an attribute:

```r

library(xml2) # v.1.1.1

# reading
x <- read_xml("<a foo='' />")
n <- xml_find_first(x, "/a")
xml_attrs(n) # named character vector of length 1

# writing
xml_set_attr(n, "foo", "bar")
xml_attrs(n) # named character vector of length 1

xml_set_attr(n, "foo", "")
xml_attrs(n) # named character vector of length 0
```
Is there another way to set the value of the attribute to the empty string?

title: How to efficiently detect parsing errors with xml2?
description:
Hi all, 

I recently had to parse tons of XML files which mostly were all right. But occasionally, there were parsing errors due to file errors or incomplete XML nodes (I know that those files shouldn't be named _valid_). And if I have an incomplete XML file, `xml2::read_xml` crashes my R instance with a seq_fault.

> *** caught segfault ***
> address 0x0, cause 'unknown'
> 
> Traceback:
>  1: .Call("xml2_doc_parse_raw", PACKAGE = "xml2", x, encoding, base_url,     as_html, options)
>  2: doc_parse_raw(x, encoding = encoding, base_url = base_url, as_html = as_html,     options = options)
>  3: read_xml.raw(raw, encoding = encoding, base_url = base_url, as_html = as_html,     options = options)
>  4: read_xml.connection(con, encoding = encoding, ..., as_html = as_html,     base_url = x, options = options)
>  5: read_xml.character(x = x, options = "RECOVER", verbose = TRUE)
>  6: xml2::read_xml(x = x, options = "RECOVER", verbose = TRUE)
>  7: doTryCatch(return(expr), name, parentenv, handler)
>  8: tryCatchOne(expr, names, parentenv, handlers[[1L]])
>  9: tryCatchList(expr, classes, parentenv, handlers)
> 10: tryCatch(xml2::read_xml(x = x, options = "RECOVER", verbose = TRUE), error = function(e) e)

I found in the {XML} package `XML::getXMLErrors`, which perfectly works in my case: Either I get an empty list (`list()`) or a list with errors describing the reason.

Because I like the idea of xml2, I was wondering whether there is a similar way in the {xml2} package? I've checked the parsing options of `xml2::read_xml` but wasn't really succesful.

Any help or advice is greatly appreciated!
Thanks!

The problem is likely that `#!/bin/bash` is hardcoded in configure. OpenBSD does not have `bash` in its base system. Even if you install a package for it, it is in `/usr/local/bin/bash`.

title: Encoding problem on Windows with non-US English locale
description:
I have various reports of problems with listing Google Sheets or specifying worksheet names or (possibly) reading Sheet data from [1] Windows and [2] non-US English locales. Examples: Spanish_Spain.1252, Danish_Denmark.1252 and ... someone in Colombia who didn't provide session info.

I think all the problematic text has been successfully processed with `httr::content(as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8")` but then a problem is introduced in `xml2::read_xml()`.

The most relevant issue is https://github.com/jennybc/googlesheets/issues/151. I apologize for some noise there -- a recent example Sheet posted seems to have a different problem. If you look there, focus on the comments from @krose. He has done a lot of digging and posed a related [question on stack overflow](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/33068063/encoding-and-raw-in-r). From his work it seems the problem might come from

[read_xml.raw(charToRaw(enc2utf8(x)), "UTF-8", ..., as_html = as_html)](https://github.com/hadley/xml2/blob/fdfd0d36683129d5a4ce72dddcd06c257e794cc5/R/xml_parse.R#L55)

title: Consider pure R node representation?
description:
``` R
make_node <- function(name, children = list(), attr = list()) {
  # Check that children is a list
  # Check that attributes is a named list

  structure(
    name = name,
    children = children,
    attr = attr,
    class = "r_xml_node"
  )
}

node <- function(name, ...) {
  parts <- list(...)
  has_names <- names(parts)

  make_node(
    name,
    children = parts[!has_names],
    attr = parts[has_names]
  )
}
```

This would make it easier to have a symmetric `as_list()` and `as_xml()`. However, we need to scope this carefully as we don't want to end up in like XML where you have two alternative representations and each function only works with one.

title: FR: as_xml()
description:
It would be awesome to have `as_xml()` to enable a roundtrip with `as_list()`.

`as_list()` has a limited scope and that would be just fine for the inverse. I'm really only interested in being able to create XML from simple R lists.

> `as_list` currently only handles the four most common types of children that an element might have:
> -  Other elements, converted to lists.
> - Attributes, stored as R attributes.
> - Text, stored as a character vector.

The `XML` package sort of has (had?) this, in the form of `XML::toHTML()`. This topic has also seen quite a bit of stackoverflow action: [How to create xml from R objects, e.g., is there a 'listToXml' function?](http://stackoverflow.com/questions/6256064/how-to-create-xml-from-r-objects-e-g-is-there-a-listtoxml-function/6256229#6256229).

title: Ambiguity about XML document versus its root node
description:
I use an example from `read_xml()` to make a small XML document two ways:
-   `read_xml()` with string input
-   `xml_new_document()` followed by several calls to `xml_add_child()`

These two paths to same destination leave you with `xml_document` objects that function differently. Is this intentional? It's pretty confusing. I think this issue might be a long-winded version of #106.

`read_xml()` says it returns an XML document. But it really returns the root node, with the class set to `c("xml_document", "xml_node")`. Which is true of _almost_ everything that inherits from `xml_document`.

``` r
library(magrittr)
library(xml2)
## taken from `read_xml()` examples
ex1 <- read_xml("<foo> <bar><baz /></bar> </foo>")
ex1
#> {xml_document}
#> <foo>
#> [1] <bar>\n  <baz/>\n</bar>
str(ex1)
#> List of 2
#>  $ node:<externalptr> 
#>  $ doc :<externalptr> 
#>  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "xml_document" "xml_node"
```

Now make the same XML by hand. Hold onto the document and the root node.

``` r
ex2_doc <- xml_new_document()
ex2_root <- ex2_doc %>%
  xml_add_child("foo") %>%
  xml_add_child("bar") %>%
  xml_add_child("baz") %>%
  xml_root()
ex2_doc
#> {xml_document}
str(ex2_doc)
#> List of 1
#>  $ doc:<externalptr> 
#>  - attr(*, "class")= chr "xml_document"
ex2_root
#> {xml_document}
#> <foo>
#> [1] <bar>\n  <baz/>\n</bar>
str(ex2_root)
#> List of 2
#>  $ node:<externalptr> 
#>  $ doc :<externalptr> 
#>  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "xml_document" "xml_node"
```

By the way, the problematic printing of `ex2_doc` above is fixed by #126. But nothing else here is. This printing problem is also noted in #106.

Up to explicit encoding, these are all the same when converted to character.

``` r
as.character(ex1)
#> [1] "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n<foo><bar><baz/></bar></foo>\n"
as.character(ex2_doc)
#> [1] "<?xml version=\"1.0\"?>\n<foo><bar><baz/></bar></foo>\n"
as.character(ex2_root)
#> [1] "<?xml version=\"1.0\"?>\n<foo><bar><baz/></bar></foo>\n"
```

As noted in #106, the fact that `ex2_doc` is an XML document (and not the root node) means that `xml_structure()` doesn't work. #126 doesn't fix this.

``` r
xml_structure(ex1)
#> <foo>
#>   <bar>
#>     <baz>
xml_structure(ex2_doc)
#> Error in UseMethod("tree_structure"): no applicable method for 'tree_structure' applied to an object of class "xml_document"
xml_structure(ex2_root)
#> <foo>
#>   <bar>
#>     <baz>
```

`as_list()` says it turns an XML document into an R list, but there's no actual method for `xml_document`. So it only works for the objects of class `xml_document` that also inherit from `xml_node`.

``` r
as_list(ex1)
#> $bar
#> $bar$baz
#> list()
as_list(ex2_doc)
#> Error in UseMethod("as_list"): no applicable method for 'as_list' applied to an object of class "xml_document"
as_list(ex2_root)
#> $bar
#> $bar$baz
#> list()
```

title: encoding of XML created de novo
description:
When I create XML _de novo_, the encoding is not explicitly set to UTF-8 when I send the document through `as.character()` or `write_xml()`, even thought the text I'm putting into the nodes is. Am I missing a way to do that? This happens automatically when XML is created by `read_xml()`.

``` r
library(xml2)

xml <- xml_new_document() %>%
  xml_add_child("root", name = "people") %>%
  xml_root()
Encoding(gabor <- "Gábor Csárdi")
#> [1] "UTF-8"
Encoding(maelle <- "Maëlle Salmon")
#> [1] "UTF-8"
xml_add_child(xml, "person", "Gábor Csárdi")
#> {xml_node}
#> <person>
y <- xml_add_child(xml, "person")
xml_text(y) <- maelle
xml
#> {xml_document}
#> <root name="people">
#> [1] <person>Gábor Csárdi</person>
#> [2] <person>Maëlle Salmon</person>
as.character(xml)
#> [1] "<?xml version=\"1.0\"?>\n<root name=\"people\"><person>Gábor Csárdi</person><person>Maëlle Salmon</person></root>\n"
xml3 <- read_xml("<root name = 'people'><person>Gábor Csárdi</person><person>Maëlle Salmon</person></root>")
as.character(xml3)
#> [1] "<?xml version=\"1.0\" encoding=\"UTF-8\"?>\n<root name=\"people\"><person>Gábor Csárdi</person><person>Maëlle Salmon</person></root>\n"
```

title: xml_text does not trim "&nbsp"

Minimal-Example: ``` require(xml2) space <- rawToChar(as.raw(c(0xc2, 0xa0))) doc <- read_xml(paste0('', space, '')) xml_text(doc, trim = TRUE) == "" # FALSE charToRaw(xml_text(doc, trim = TRUE)) #[1] c2 a0 ``` Workaround: `stringi::stri_trim_both(xml_text(doc, trim = TRUE))` or `stringr::str_trim`

title: xml_integer() does not return integer
description:
For example:
```
x <- read_xml("<plot><point x='1' y='2' /><point x='2' y='1' /></plot>")
xml_integer(xml_find_all(x, "//@x")) %>% is
[1] "numeric"        "vector"         "atomic"         "vectorORfactor"
```
The culprit might be in xml_text.R:
```
#' @export
xml_integer.xml_nodeset <- function(x) {
  vapply(x, xml_integer, numeric(1))
}
```
Where changing `numeric(1)` for `integer(1)` fixes it. It seem the unit test for xml_integer is passing because it uses expect_equal instead of expect_identical (but I am just getting familiar with testthat so I may be completely wrong on this):
```
test_that("xml_integer() returns an integer vector", {
  x <- read_xml("<plot><point x='1' y='2' /><point x='2' y='1' /></plot>")

  expect_equal(xml_integer(xml_find_all(x, "//@x")),
    c(1L, 2L))
})
```

title: Feature request: attach namespace to an xml document
description:
This is something you mentioned yourself here:

https://github.com/hadley/xml2/issues/24#issuecomment-93810992

From where I sit, this would be a very handy thing.

Related question: could the result of `xml_ns()` be attached to a new xml document by default? Or just available by default? Or could that behaviour be requestable?

Consider this example from [here](http://www.edankert.com/defaultnamespaces.html):

```
x <- read_xml('
<catalog xmlns="http://www.edankert.com/examples/">
  <cd>
    <artist>Sufjan Stevens</artist>
    <title>Illinois</title>
    <src>http://www.sufjan.com/</src>
  </cd>
  <cd>
    <artist>Stoat</artist>
    <title>Future come and get me</title>
    <src>http://www.stoatmusic.com/</src>
  </cd>
  <cd>
    <artist>The White Stripes</artist>
    <title>Get behind me satan</title>
    <src>http://www.whitestripes.com/</src>
  </cd>
</catalog>')
```

Due to the use of a default namespace, this does not work:

```
> xml_find_all(x, "//cd")
{xml_nodeset (0)}
```

So I inspect the namespace.

```
> xml_ns(x)
d1 <-> http://www.edankert.com/examples/
```

OK now I have hope I can use the `d1` prefix to specify default namespace. I'm usually happy to accept a default prefix like this.

```
> xml_find_all(x, "//d1:cd")
xmlXPathEval: evaluation failed
{xml_nodeset (0)}
Warning message:
In node_find_all(x$node, x$doc, xpath = xpath, nsMap = ns) :
  Undefined namespace prefix [1219]
```

Sad. But this does work:

```
> xml_find_all(x, "//d1:cd", xml_ns(x))
{xml_nodeset (3)}
[1] <cd>\n              <artist>Sufjan Stevens</artist>\n              <title>Illi ...
[2] <cd>\n              <artist>Stoat</artist>\n              <title>Future come a ...
[3] <cd>\n              <artist>The White Stripes</artist>\n              <title>G …
```

Could any of that be made easier?

I posted [this question in StackOverflow](https://stackoverflow.com/posts/35144449/edit). I am trying to scrape data off tens of thousands of html files using R. [Here's a sample file](https://www.dropbox.com/s/ztnzm35ri2lxszl/sample_file.html?dl=0) that one should use to reproduce the problem I describe below.

I am trying to use the xml2 package. The problem I am getting relates to encoding. What is killing me is the fact that this problem was not happening with the XML package. Here's what I am doing:

```
library(xml2)    

# paths to input and output files
input.file = 'C:/tmp/sample_file.html'
out.file = 'C:/tmp/output_from_xml2.csv'

# read html file as string
input = readChar(input.file, file.info(input.file)$size)    
    # small hack; consider pre-processing all files and get rid of this hack
    input = gsub(pattern = ' ?', x = input, perl = T, rep = ' ')     

# parse file
tree = read_html(input)

# the relevant tables
tables = xml_find_all(tree, '//table[@id="Tabela_Itens"]')

# the table I am interested in
mytable = tables[[6]]

# extract table
cells = xml_find_all(mytable, './/td')
info = data.frame(matrix(xml_text(cells, trim = T), ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# print -- note the gibberish characters
info[1:5, 4]

 [1] "Licitante"                                                
 [2] "LIDERANÃƒâ€¡A LIMPEZA E CONSERVAÃƒâ€¡ÃƒÆ’O LTDA."         
 [3] "ARTLIMP SERVICOS LTDA"                                    
 [4] "DINÃƒâ€šMICA SERVIÃƒâ€¡OS GERAIS LTDA"                    
 [5] "Servnac TerceirizaÃƒÂ§ÃƒÂ£o Limitada"                     
```

I tried tweaking the line

```
# parse file
tree = read_html(input)
```

by passing the argument `encoding`, but no luck.
### `sessionInfo()`:

```
> sessionInfo()
R version 3.2.3 (2015-12-10)
Platform: x86_64-w64-mingw32/x64 (64-bit)
Running under: Windows 7 x64 (build 7601) Service Pack 1

```
### side note: solution using XML

My first choice was to use the XML package. All good, [except for the memory leak](https://github.com/omegahat/XML/blob/master/Docs/MemoryManagement.pdf), which makes it infeasible to loop over my tens of thousands of files. There doesn't seem to be a simple solution for that. [This document](https://github.com/omegahat/XML/blob/master/Docs/MemoryManagement.pdf), despite all it's good intentions, is not that helpful. 

The solution using XML however does rend correct characters:

```
library(XML)

#
input.file = 'C:/tmp/sample_file.html'
out.file = 'C:/tmp/output_from_xml.csv'

# read html file as string
input = readChar(input.file, file.info(input.file)$size)    
    # small hack; consider pre-processing all files and get rid of this hack
    input = gsub(pattern = ' ?', x = input, perl = T, rep = ' ')     

# parse file
tree = htmlParse(input, encoding = 'UTF-8')

# the relevant tables
tables = getNodeSet(tree, '//table[@id="Tabela_Itens"]')

# the table I am interested in
mytable = tables[[6]]

# extract table
info = readHTMLTable(mytable, colClasses = 'character', header = T)

# print -- that's what I want: latin characters are displayed correctly
info[1:5, 4]

 [1] LIDERANÇA LIMPEZA E CONSERVAÇÃO LTDA.             
 [2] ARTLIMP SERVICOS LTDA                             
 [3] DINÂMICA SERVIÇOS GERAIS LTDA                     
 [4] Servnac Terceirização Limitada                    
 [5] SATO-SAN SERVIÇOS S/C LTDA. - EPP.                
15 Levels: APPA SOLUÇÕES EMPRESARIAIS LTDA-ME ...
```

(The two solutions also have small differences -- the header; one is in character, the other has a factor; but I do not worry about those.)

title: How to ignore "insignificant whitespace"?
description:
I'm using the term "insignificant whitespace" as defined in [What You Need to Know About Whitespace in XML](http://www.oracle.com/technetwork/articles/wang-whitespace-092897.html):

> _Insignificant whitespace_ is used when editing XML documents for readability. These whitespaces are typically not intended for inclusion in the delivery of the document.

Consider XML that has been formatted for human eyeballs. `xml2` can read it w/o error and well-formed XPATH expressions do what one expects. But once you use `as_list()` or try to write it back out with `write_xml()`, you learn there are problems with whitespace.

``` r
cd <- read_xml("http://www.xmlfiles.com/examples/cd_catalog.xml")
```

Targetted queries work fine:

``` r
xml_find_all(cd, ".//TITLE")
#> {xml_nodeset (26)}
#>  [1] <TITLE>Empire Burlesque</TITLE>
#>  [2] <TITLE>Hide your heart</TITLE>
#>  [3] <TITLE>Greatest Hits</TITLE>
#>  [4] <TITLE>Still got the blues</TITLE>
#>  [5] <TITLE>Eros</TITLE>
#>  [6] <TITLE>One night only</TITLE>
#>  [7] <TITLE>Sylvias Mother</TITLE>
#>  [8] <TITLE>Maggie May</TITLE>
#>  [9] <TITLE>Romanza</TITLE>
#> [10] <TITLE>When a man loves a woman</TITLE>
#> [11] <TITLE>Black angel</TITLE>
#> [12] <TITLE>1999 Grammy Nominees</TITLE>
#> [13] <TITLE>For the good times</TITLE>
#> [14] <TITLE>Big Willie style</TITLE>
#> [15] <TITLE>Tupelo Honey</TITLE>
#> [16] <TITLE>Soulsville</TITLE>
#> [17] <TITLE>The very best of</TITLE>
#> [18] <TITLE>Stop</TITLE>
#> [19] <TITLE>Bridge of Spies</TITLE>
#> [20] <TITLE>Private Dancer</TITLE>
#> ...
```

But `as_list()` reveals some problems

``` r
str(as_list(cd), max.level = 1, list.len = 5)
#> List of 53
#>  $   : chr "\n  "
#>  $ CD:List of 13
#>   .. [list output truncated]
#>  $   : chr "\n  "
#>  $ CD:List of 13
#>   .. [list output truncated]
#>  $   : chr "\n  "
#>   [list output truncated]
```

and indeed you can't invert things with `write_xml()`

``` r
write(cd, "cd_catalog.xml")
#> Error in cat(list(...), file, sep, fill, labels, append): argument 1 (type 'list') cannot be handled by 'cat'
```

title: Excessive depth in document error causing issues for dependent package rNOMADS
description:
I maintain the rNOMADS package, which relies on xml2 to parse large lists of web-hosted files.  Unfortunately, attempts to retrieve some file list fails with

```
Error: Excessive depth in document: 256 use XML_PARSE_HUGE option [1]
```

I have spent a great deal of time attempting to reset this depth in order to permit my users to download the data they need.  However, I believe this depth is hard coded and thus can't be changed.  This is a serious issue for the proper functioning of my package.  The only work around I can provide is to ask my users to download a forked version of xml2 that is not available on CRAN:

```
library(drat)
drat:::add("shabbychef")
install.packages('xml2'
```

Would it be possible to implement shabbychef's fix in the official xml2 repository, so I can easily make it available to my users?
To reproduce error:

```
library(xml2)
library(lubridate)

date.today <- format(now(tz = "UTC"), "%Y%m%d")
url <- paste0("http://nomads.ncep.noaa.gov/cgi-bin/filter_rap.pl?dir=%2Frap.", date.today)
xml2::read_html(url)
```

  as_list %>%

title: Feature Request: Coersion to/from xml_nodeset and XML classes
description:
Apologies if this is already possible (if so then updates to the documentation would be helpful).

It would be helpful if there were ways to coerce vectors and lists into `xml_nodeset` objects without going through `as.character() %>% read_html() %>% html_nodes()`. 

There are two specific use cases I have for this:
1. When accessing REST APIs, it is not uncommon to have arbitrary blobs of HTML embedded in the JSON. I would like to be able to coerce a vector or list of these HTML blobs into the `xml_nodeset` class so that I can use all the wonderful extraction tools of `xml2` and `rvest` on them. Creating a loop or `apply` function creates an awful lot of processing overhead. 
2. Until `xml2` gains XML create/modify functions and something comparable to `XMLtoDataFrame`, I will still need to access the tools in the `XML` package, and right now, that means turning my lovely `xml_nodeset` into characters, parsing them as XML, setting a root node, etc. It would really be very convenient to be able to just coerce an `xml_nodeset` into the appropriate XML object. This is relevant to `xml2` because `xml2` will handle HTTPS connections without supervision, but `XML` needs help. 

I think both use cases get addressed nicely with coercion methods and the appropriate `as` functions. I'm hoping that this shouldn't be too hard to implement since the classes from both packages seem to be special kinds of lists. 

I would also be very happy to be enlightened if there is already a less obvious way of accomplishing these tasks.

title: difficulty forming tbl_df from XML
description:
This may very well be user error, but I'd love to understand what I am doing wrong.

Example below starts with XML inspired by the Google Sheets "cell feed" (but greatly simplified). My goal is to get a `tbl_df` with one row per cell.

I am trying to use the pipe operator and a `dplyr`-ish workflow but I am puzzled by an unexpected variable that is an XML node set. If I eliminate an intermediate step, I even get a fatal error.

What am I doing wrong?

``` r
suppressPackageStartupMessages(library("dplyr"))
library("xml2")

x <- read_xml('
<feed>
  <title type="text">Africa</title>
  <author>
    <name>gspreadr</name>
    <email>gspreadr@gmail.com</email>
  </author>
  <entry>
    <title type="text">A1</title>
    <content type="text">country</content>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <title type="text">B1</title>
    <content type="text">continent</content>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <title type="text">A2</title>
    <content type="text">Algeria</content>
  </entry>
  <entry>
    <title type="text">B2</title>
    <content type="text">Africa</content>
  </entry>
</feed>
')

## get a nodeset containing the 'entry' nodes
x1 <- x %>%
  xml_find_all("//entry")

## then get the text of the title nodes
x2 <- x1 %>%
  xml_find_all(".//title") %>%
  xml_text()
x2 %>% str
#>  chr [1:4] "A1" "B1" "A2" "B2"
## it's a plain vanilla character vector YAY

## make a tbl_df from text in the title and content nodes
x3 <- x1 %>%
  data_frame(cell = xml_find_all(., ".//title") %>% xml_text(),
             value = xml_find_all(., ".//content") %>% xml_text())
x3
#> Source: local data frame [4 x 3]
#> 
#>               . cell     value
#> 1 <S3:xml_node>   A1   country
#> 2 <S3:xml_node>   B1 continent
#> 3 <S3:xml_node>   A2   Algeria
#> 4 <S3:xml_node>   B2    Africa
## what's up with this first variable `.` and how do I suppress its creation?
x3$`.` %>% class
#> [1] "xml_nodeset"
x3 %>% glimpse
#> Observations: 4
#> Variables:
#> Error in prettyNum(.Internal(format(x, trim, digits, nsmall, width, 3L, : first argument must be atomic
## glimpse does not like this variable name?

## attempt to make same tbl_df but w/o the intermediate x1 object
x4 <- x %>%
  dplyr::data_frame(cell = xml_find_all(., "//entry//title") %>% xml_text(),
                    value = xml_find_all(., "//entry//content") %>% xml_text())
#> Error in data_frame_(lazyeval::lazy_dots(...)): arguments imply differing number of rows: 2, 4, 4
## this doesn't work at all

## get rid of the pipe SUCCESS
x5 <- data_frame(cell = xml_find_all(x1, ".//title") %>% xml_text(),
                 value = xml_find_all(x1, ".//content") %>% xml_text())
x5
#> Source: local data frame [4 x 2]
#> 
#>   cell     value
#> 1   A1   country
#> 2   B1 continent
#> 3   A2   Algeria
#> 4   B2    Africa
```

title: Iterating over xml_children returns externalptr rather than nodeset
